body_mdx:
## 1. Kinematic Mechanics of Elastic Deflection Strain wave gearing achieves zero-backlash torque multiplication up to 160:1 in a single coaxial stage through continuous elastic deformation. {{ FIGURE_0 }} An elliptical cam (the wave generator) inserted into a thin-walled flexible cup (the flexspline) deflects the cup so its external teeth mesh with the internal teeth of a rigid ring (the circular spline) at two opposing diametrical lobes.
Material Alloy
SNCM439 / 40CrNiMoA Alloy Steel
Tensile: 1,100 MPa • Yield: 950 MPa
Tooth Meshing Pitch
Module m = 0.3mm (200 teeth)
2-tooth difference yields 100:1 reduction
 {{ FIGURE_1 }} ## 2. Flexspline Diaphragm Fatigue Mechanics Because the cup rotates relative to the elliptical wave generator, every point along the cup wall undergoes two complete tension-compression strain cycles per revolution. The peak cyclic bending stress is given by: $$\sigma_b = \frac{E \cdot t}{2 \cdot R^2} \cdot w_0$$ Where $t$ is wall thickness ($0.35 \text{ mm}$), $R$ is nominal radius, and $w_0$ is radial deflection. Controlling surface roughness to $R_a < 0.2 \mu\text{m}$ along the cup root radius is essential to eliminate micro-crack nucleation sites.
